title: Rendering: SSR, CSR, prerendering and choosing an adapter

videos.script:
Every page so far has been rendered the same way. {{modes}} The server writes the HTML, and the browser takes it over. This lesson tries the other ways, and measures what each one sends.

First the planner needs a real server. {{node}} One adapter, one build, and a Node program you can run. Its first form fails with a four oh three. {{csrf}} That refusal is a protection against other sites posting forms in your name, and the fix is to tell the server its own address, not to switch the check off.

Then the About page tries three options. {{ssr}} With no server rendering, it arrives empty. {{csr}} With no JavaScript, it arrives whole and ships no script at all. {{prerender}} And prerendered, it becomes a file written once, at build time.

Last, the adapter that writes only files, {{choosing}} and the question that decides which adapter a project needs: where does the data live?
